adjudicated_text: धी॒ती वा॒ ये अन॑यन्वा॒चो अग्रं॒ मन॑सा वा॒ ये ऽव॑दन्नृ॒तानि॑ । ॥ १ ॥
adjudication: Three independent readers agreed EXACTLY on the accent layer: 6 anudatta + 4 svarita = 10, with identical (word_index, aksara_index, type) tuples for all 10 marks (verified programmatically). All three also independently found the same hard case: the sixth anudatta bar is set ~14-16 px BELOW the other five (y2076-2086 vs y2059-2073) because the printer had to clear the vocalic-R hook of the N+NR conjunct. S1 corroborated the habit on line 3 of the same leaf, where bars under TR and VR are dropped the same way. Two aksara identities were disputed, both ADJUDICATED FROM THE SCAN by side-by-side composite against controls taken from the same printed line: (1) word 4: AYAM (S1) vs AGRAM (S2, S3). Adopted AGRAM. The disputed glyph was composited against the certain YA of word 3 on the same line: the certain YA is a compact left bowl with a thin crescent counter joining the stem horizontally at the foot, whereas the disputed glyph has an open upper-left hook plus a prominent bold diagonal descending below the body line - a subscript RA. Majority and image agree. (2) word 3: ANAYADVACO (S1, S2) vs ANAYANVACO (S3). Adopted ANAYANVACO, OVERRIDING the 2-1 majority. The conjunct at x966-1070 was composited against plain NA (x1550-1628), plain DA (x2195-2262) and plain VA (x2128-2196) from the same line. The conjunct's upper member is a left blob with a horizontal bar running right and white above it - identical to plain NA - while plain DA on this line is a hook curving down-left with a rounded terminal and NO rightward bar. The lower member matches plain VA. S1 had justified DVA by claiming the upper member repeats the left wedge plus rightward bar of the plain DA, but the DA on this line has no rightward bar at all; that feature is diagnostic of NA. Both S1 and S2 had already flagged this conjunct as their least certain glyph. Neither disputed locus affects any mark tuple.

readers.initial_text: धी॒ती वा॒ ये अन॑यद्वा॒चो अयं॒ मन॑सा वा॒ ये ऽव॑दन्नृ॒तानि॑ । ॥ १ ॥
readers.dissent: Read word 4 as AYAM and word 3 as ANAYADVACO. Both OVERRULED from the scan by composite against same-line controls (see adjudication).
readers.y_bands: All y in leaf-block coordinates (text block = crop (482,362)-(3618,5448) of the 4000 px leaf; block 3136x5086). Measured by row-ink projection at ink threshold 140; the verso bleed-through ghost is never darker than gray 183 anywhere in these bands, so ghost and ink are fully separable and no band boundary rests on a judgement call. LINE-ABOVE BAR BAND: line 1 is the short centred ॥ ओं ॥ and its ink lies only in y1737-1854; its own bar band would fall near y1885-1900, and I measured y1855-1914 as ZERO ink at every x. On this line the line-above trap is therefore empirically absent - nothing from line 1 can reach my bands. MY SVARITA BAND: y1914-1951 (the four upright strokes begin at y1914-1920 and stand on the sirorekha at 1951, with clean white above them). MY SIROREKHA: y1950-1967; row-ink peak 2119 px at y1963, solid 1953-1966. MY GLYPH BODY: y1968-2032. MY DESCENDER/SUBSCRIPT ZONE: y2033-2058 (the द tail in वदन्नृ, the ृ hook). MY OWN ANUDATTA BAR BAND: y2058-2072 - five bars at 2059-2068, 2061-2069, 2061-2069, 2061-2071, 2062-2072 - plus ONE bar dropped to y2076-2086 because the ृ hook of न्नृ occupies the normal band there. NEXT LINE (line 3): above-headline band y2091-2126, sirorekha y2127-2143, body y2144-2209, descender zone y2210-2237, its own bar band y2238-2261 (ordinary bars 2239-2250, and two bars dropped to 2250-2261 under the ृ of तृ and वृ - the same displacement rule, which is what corroborates my sixth bar). Line pitch 177 px (sirorekha centre 1958 -> 2135); the bar band sits +103..+114 below its own sirorekha, +118..+128 when a ृ pushes it down.
readers.boundary_interpretation: WORDS. I took word boundaries from where the sirorekha itself breaks, sampled at rows 1956/1960/1963. Inter-word gaps measure 39-51 px; gaps between aksaras inside a word measure 6-23 px, so the two classes do not overlap. Printed words with x spans: 0 धीती 190-409 (the 223-229 break is internal to ध, whose curl and right stem separate below the headline), 1 वा 449-566, 2 ये 607-679, 3 अनयद्वाचो 720-1210, 4 अयं 1249-1431, 5 मनसा 1470-1744, 6 वा 1784-1903, 7 ये 1942-2015, 8 ऽवदन्नृतानि 2061-2562, 9 । 2606-2622, 10 ॥ १ ॥ 2875-3096. The avagraha ऽ (2061-2109) is separated from the following व by only 11 px at headline level (23 px in the body zone), i.e. an inter-aksara gap and not a word space, so I treat ऽवदन्नृतानि as one printed word (word_index 8). The avagraha is a sign of elision, not an aksara, so it gets no aksara_index: inside word 8 the indices are व=0, द=1, न्नृ=2, ता=3, नि=4. AKSARAS. Boundaries come from a column-ink profile of the body zone y1972-2032 - below the sirorekha, so the headline cannot bridge them. Runs: 195-252 + 269-287 (धी), 306-358 + 377-395 (ती) | 461-517 + 540-556 (वा) | 617-674 (ये) | 723-812 (अ), 824-887 (न), 902-959 (य), 966-1036 + 1054-1070 (द्वा), 1092-1157 + 1180-1197 (चो) | 1252-1343 (अ), 1354-1422 (यं) | 1477-1547 (म), 1557-1620 (न), 1627-1696 + 1714-1731 (सा) | 1796-1852 + 1874-1890 (वा) | 1951-2009 (ये) | 2061-2109 (ऽ), 2133-2189 (व), 2201-2253 (द), 2259-2332 (न्नृ), 2346-2401 + 2421-2441 (ता), 2461-2479 + 2492-2555 (नि). MARKS NEAR A BOUNDARY - side assigned, and why. (a) svarita x866-877 in word 3: it stands over the right stem of न, whose body run is 824-887; the next aksara य does not start until 902, behind a 14 px empty valley (888-901). Assigned to न, not य. (b) svarita x1601-1613 in मनसा: over the right stem of न (1557-1620); स starts at 1627. Assigned to न. (c) svarita x2537-2548 in word 8: over the न of नि. The i-matra stroke is set to the LEFT (2461-2479) and the न to the right (2492-2555), but the two are one aksara नि, so the mark is interior to it; ता ends at 2441 and the danda does not begin until 2606. Assigned to नि. (d) anudatta x1380-1419 in अयं: it sits under य (1354-1422), which also carries the anusvara dot at 1398-1421 directly above it. अ ends at 1343. Assigned to यं; I note explicitly that the bar and the dot are on the same aksara and are two different signs. (e) anudatta x2293-2329 in word 8: under the न्नृ conjunct (2259-2332); द ends at 2253 and ता does not start until 2346. Assigned to न्नृ. (f) anudatta x996-1032 in word 3: under the द्व part of द्वा (966-1036, with its a-stem at 1054-1070); य ends at 959. Assigned to द्वा. No mark straddles a word space, and no mark lies closer to a neighbouring aksara's ink than to its own.
readers.notes: MAGNIFICATION. I worked from the two supplied 1:1 segment crops, then re-rendered my own ruled windows from the 4000 px leaf via crop_atharvaveda_leaf.find_text_block / leaf_path: eight windows of 420x194 block px at 3.6x, then targeted zooms at 4.2-9.4x and one 16.7x view of the न्न stack. Beyond roughly 2x this is interpolation, and I used it only for spatial judgement, never as new detail. Every count is from measurement rather than from the rendered picture: 8-connected component extraction on the leaf block at ink thresholds 90 / 110 / 140 / 170 / 190, plus row and column ink profiles. The mark inventory is identical at thresholds 110 and 170, so nothing here depends on where I set the threshold. REJECTED FALSE POSITIVES - by shape, not by position. (1) Six wide curved matras above the headline, centres x257, x365, x638, x1155, x1972, x2492, measuring 53-72 px across and 28-34 px tall: the ी of धी and of ती, the े of both ये, the ो of चो, the ि of नि. Wide curved shapes, not narrow strokes, so not svarita. (2) The mark at x1398-1421, y1924-1949: w24, h25, aspect 0.96, ink fill 0.70, diamond-shaped, and it does not touch the sirorekha. An anusvara on यं of अयं. Round dot about as wide as it is tall, so not svarita - even though it sits directly above an anudatta bar and could be read as a paired accent. (3) The descender at x2249-2266, y2030-2057, h27, aspect 1.5: the diagonal tail of द in वदन्नृ. It runs out of the glyph body with no white gap and tapers, so not a detached flat dash. (4) The descender at x2301-2343, y2030-2074, h45, aspect 0.96: the ृ hook of न्नृ - exactly the vocalic-r false positive the brief names, a curved hook rather than a straight dash. (5) Eight small stubs clipped at the body-zone floor near x1192, 1665, 1849, 1886, 2183, 2433, 2550, 3004: all 2-6 px tall and continuous with the glyph body above them, i.e. glyph feet, not detached bars. (6) Faint smudges that appear only at thresholds 170-190, at x2074 (y2068-2073) and x2535 (y2072-2081): both roundish (aspect 1.0-2.7) and both gone at threshold 140, whereas every real bar is solid at threshold 90. Verso bleed-through, rejected. THE SIXTH ANUDATTA - the one real judgement call, and how I settled it. The bar at x2293-2329 sits at y2076-2086, about 14 px below the band the other five occupy, and at threshold 140 it merges with the ृ hook of न्नृ into a single component. At threshold 90 it separates cleanly: w35, h8, aspect 4.4, 236 ink px - the same size, shape and density class as the five undisputed bars (w33-37, h6-9, aspect 3.9-5.5, 193-265 ink px). It cannot come from the line above: line 1 is the short centred ॥ ओं ॥, nowhere near x2311, and y1855-1914 is empty at every x. It cannot come from line 3, whose sirorekha does not begin until y2127 and whose own bar band lies at y2238-2261. Decisive corroboration from the print's own habit: on line 3 the bars under तृ (x88-121) and वृ (x1226-1260) are likewise dropped to y2250-2261 while its ordinary bars sit at y2239-2250. This fount drops the anudatta clear of a ृ hook, so I count this one. Without it the answer would be 5 anudatta; I record the displacement explicitly so the disagreement, if any, is locatable. READINGS I HAD TO WORK FOR. The 1856 standalone अ does read as ऋ or श्र to a modern eye (brief's fount note); I read it as अ at x723-812 and x1252-1343, and the two forms are identical to each other and to the अ of the running head. Two stacked conjuncts needed comparison against unambiguous letters elsewhere on the same scan rather than guesswork: x966-1070 I read द्वा, because its upper member repeats the left wedge plus rightward bar of the plain द at x2201-2253 and its lower member repeats the closed loop of the plain व at x2133-2189; x2259-2332 I read न्नृ, because at 16.7x it is visibly two identical न hook-and-bar forms stacked on a shared right stem. I also checked the first aksara against line 3's ध in धेनोः (x2065-2135), which shows the same left flag, 3-shaped double curl and right stem, confirming धी and not some other flagged letter. WHAT I DID NOT DO. I consulted no text, edition, translation or web resource, and I did not open the detector scripts, the transcription data, the baseline run file, or any other reader's directory. धीती and अनयद्वाचो are what the ink shows; I did not bend them toward any remembered Atharvaveda wording, and I did not try to make the accent pattern satisfy a grammatical expectation. UNRESOLVED. Nothing material. The ॥ १ ॥ at x2875-3096 is set off to the right with 253 px of space after the single danda at x2606-2622, and I have kept both as printed. Residual risk, stated plainly: the identity of the two stacked conjuncts is an inference from letterform comparison at a resolution close to the scan's limit, but neither affects any mark count or any carrier assignment.

readers.dissent: Read word 3 as ANAYADVACO. OVERRULED from the scan; S2 had itself listed this conjunct as unclear, read as DVA by elimination.
readers.y_bands: All y in leaf-block coordinates of the 4000px raster (find_text_block box 482,362-3618,5448; block 3136x5086). Measured on the source raster by full-width row-ink projection at thresholds 128/170 plus 8-connected component extents, not eyeballed off a render. LINE ABOVE (a short centred heading, inked only over x 941-2353, 225 inked columns, no sirorekha): ink y 1738-1861. ITS BAR BAND: none - the entire gutter y 1862-1913 is blank, 0 inked pixels at threshold 170 apart from 1-3px paper specks at y 1897-1905. So on this line there is no line-above bar band that could be mistaken for my svarita. MY SVARITA / SUPRA-HEADLINE BAND: y 1914-1951 (holds my four svarita strokes plus the five wide matras and the one anusvara). MY SIROREKHA: y 1952-1971 (row ink 980-2102, peak 2102 at y 1962-1964). MY GLYPH BODY: y 1971-2035 (row ink falls from ~1400 to 45 by y 2036). Two body descenders run lower: the tail of da at x 2232-2265 to y 2056, and the vocalic-r hook at x 2300-2344 to y 2074. MY OWN BAR BAND: y 2058-2073 - five anudatta bars at y 2058/2059 to 2068/2073 with a 3px downward drift left-to-right across the line; a sixth bar is displaced down to y 2077-2087 because the vocalic-r hook of the na-nr aksara occupies its normal slot. NEXT LINE: its supra-headline band starts at y 2091 (tallest members top out 2091-2098) and its sirorekha is y 2128-2147. Rows y 2088-2090 carry 0 ink, cleanly separating my displaced bar from the next line's band. Line pitch (my sirorekha centre 1962 to the next line's 2136) = 174 px.
readers.boundary_interpretation: WORD SEGMENTATION. I took the sirorekha runs at y 1958 and y 1962 as primary evidence and cross-checked against body-column runs over y 1975-2030. The sirorekha breaks fall into two clearly separated populations: intra-word letter joins of 4-12 px, and inter-word gaps of 38-49 px. Applying a 38px floor the line segments into nine words plus punctuation: [0] dhiitii x 187-409, [1] vaa x 449-567, [2] ye x 607-679, [3] anayadvaacho x 720-1210, [4] agram x 1249-1431, [5] manasaa x 1470-1744, [6] vaa x 1784-1903, [7] ye x 1941-2015, [8] avagraha+vadannrtaani x 2065-2562; then danda x 2606-2622, double-danda x 2875-2913, numeral 1 x 2961-3009, double-danda x 3059-3096. The avagraha (x 2065-2110) is separated from the preceding ye by 49px but from the following va by only 10px, so I attached it to the following word as printed, giving word [8]. word_index runs over those nine Devanagari words only; the danda, double-dandas and verse numeral are punctuation and get no word index (no mark falls near them). AKSARA INDEXING. I enumerate printed glyph cells left to right. Inside word [8] the avagraha is counted as aksara_index 0, so va=1, da=2, na-nr=3, taa=4, ni=5. If a comparison convention excludes the avagraha from the aksara count, subtract 1 from every aksara_index in word [8]. MARKS NEAR A BOUNDARY. This print sets the anudatta bar under the left-of-centre part of its aksara, and the svarita tick directly over that aksara's right-hand vertical stem; every assignment below is a containment test against measured glyph columns. x 226 (bar 207-245): dhii occupies x 195-290, tii x 306-396 - wholly inside dhii, not near a boundary. x 494 (bar 476-512): the single-aksara word vaa occupies x 461-556; unambiguous. x 871 (tick 866-877): na occupies x 820-892 with its own stem at x 872-880, and the sirorekha breaks at x 893-896 before ya. The tick stands over na's stem, 22px clear of the break, so it is na's and not ya's. x 1014 (bar 995-1033): ya occupies x 897-963, the dva conjunct x 968-1070 (its aa stem 1053-1070). The bar lies entirely right of ya's right edge and its centre is within 12px of dva's centre. This is the closest of the six bars; assigned to dva. x 1400 (bar 1379-1420): a occupies x 1250-1350, gram x 1353-1428. The bar is wholly right of 1353, and the anusvara dot of gram (x 1397-1422) stands directly above it at the same x, so dot and bar belong to the same aksara. Assigned to gram. x 1607 (tick 1601-1613): inside manasaa (ma 1477-1550, na 1554-1620, sa 1626-1697, aa 1713-1731) the tick falls inside na. x 1828 (bar 1810-1848): the single-aksara word vaa occupies x 1796-1890; unambiguous. x 2177 (tick 2171-2184): va occupies x 2132-2198 with its stem at x 2178-2188 and da begins at x 2199. The tick is over va's stem, so va's and not da's. x 2311 (bar 2290-2330): the na-nr aksara occupies roughly x 2270-2330 and owns the vocalic-r hook at x 2300-2344; da is x 2199-2266 and its tail ends at x 2266 / y 2056. The bar lies entirely right of 2266 and directly under the na-nr cell, so it is na-nr's and not da's. x 2542 (tick 2536-2549): ni occupies x 2461-2556 - the short-i matra arc is x 2463-2522 and na's right stem is x 2537-2555. The tick stands over that stem and is 50px clear of the danda at x 2606, so it is ni's, and it is the last mark on the line.
readers.notes: MAGNIFICATION AND METHOD. I read the two supplied 1568px segment crops, re-rendered the same line at 4 segments with scripts/crop_atharvaveda_line.py, then cut my own PIL crops of the same line at x3 to x10 (LANCZOS) around every candidate. All positions and sizes reported here were measured on the source raster itself (leaf 4000x5959; find_text_block box 482,362-3618,5448; block 3136x5086) via row-ink projection, per-row/per-column ink maps, and 8-connected component extents at thresholds 128, 150 and 175. ACCEPTED MARKS. Six anudatta: flat dashes 36-40px wide by 9-11px tall (aspect about 3.7:1) at x 207-245, 476-512, 995-1033, 1379-1420, 1808-1849 in the band y 2058-2073, plus one at x 2290-2330 / y 2077-2087. Four svarita: upright strokes 10-13px wide by 29-37px tall (aspect about 1:3) at x 866-877, 1601-1613, 2171-2184, 2536-2549, all rising from the top of my sirorekha into the band y 1914-1951. All ten are stable across thresholds 128-175. REJECTED FALSE POSITIVES, BY SHAPE. (1) x 2300-2344, y 2036-2074, 45x39 - a curved hook, the vocalic-r descender of the na-nr aksara: rejected as anudatta because it is curved and 39px tall, i.e. taller than wide, and runs continuously up into the glyph body with no white gap. It is why the sixth real bar sits 15px lower than the other five. At threshold 175 hook and bar merge into one component; at 128 and 150 they are separate, and the raw pixel map shows a clear light row at y 2075-2076 between them, so the bar is a genuinely separate mark. (2) x 2232-2265, y 2032-2056, 34x24 - the diagonal tail of the da in vadan-, continuous with its glyph body, no white gap, diagonal not flat. (3) Five wide curved matras above the headline, all rejected on width: x 228-285 (ii of dhii), 337-392 (ii of tii), 608-668 (e of ye), 1120-1191 (o of cho), 2462-2523 (short i of ni) - 55 to 72px across, against 10-13px for a svarita. The control is dhiitii, where the ii is printed as a broad arch above the headline whose right leg descends to the baseline; none of my four ticks carries any arch. (4) x 1397-1422, y 1924-1947, 26x24 - the anusvara of gram: a diamond dot about as wide as tall, not an upright stroke. (5) A faint horizontal smudge that appeared under ye / avagraha around x 2058-2096, y 2037-2047 in a LANCZOS render: the raw pixel map of x 2040-2115, y 2034-2059 is entirely blank (all values above 190). A resampling artefact on paper texture, not ink. (6) At threshold 175 three specks appear in the bar band - x 2157-2163 (7x6), x 2530-2538 (9x8), x 2556-2562 (7x4); all far below the 20-45px anudatta width and all gone at 150. Speckle. (7) Verso show-through is visible between the danda at x 2606-2622 and the double-danda at x 2875-2913; it is grey, unfocused and mirrored, and carries no mark. LINE ATTRIBUTION. The brief's central trap does not bite on this line: the line above is a short centred heading confined to x 941-2353 with no sirorekha, and the gutter between it and mine (y 1862-1913) carries zero ink at threshold 170, so nothing in my supra-headline band can be a bar from the line above. Symmetrically, the next line's supra band does not start until y 2091 with rows y 2088-2090 empty, so my displaced bar at y 2077-2087 cannot belong to it - and it is flat, whereas anything of the next line's in that band would be one of its own upright strokes or a wide matra. UNCLEAR (2), both glyph-identity doubts rather than accent doubts. (a) The stacked conjunct at x 968-1050 read as dva: the lower member is plainly va (closed loop plus stem), the upper member is a reduced half-form I read as da by elimination and it could conceivably be another dental. (b) The stacked conjunct at x 2270-2330 read as n-na: two na-like members on one stem with the vocalic r below; at the 2024px native resolution the upper member's identity is at the limit of the raster. Neither doubt changes the mark count or the carrier assignment, since in both cases the mark sits under the single stacked cell. The standalone vowel at x 722-817 and x 1250-1350 is read as a per the brief's fount note, though to a modern eye it reads as vocalic r or shra. I consulted no external text, edition, database or web resource, and I did not read or run the detector or binder scripts, nor anything under data/transcriptions/atharvaveda_bsb_1856/, nor any sibling reader directory. Where memory of the Atharvaveda suggested a reading I checked it against the ink; what is reported is what the ink shows. Spacing note: text_devanagari uses single spaces throughout, but as printed the gap between the single danda (x 2606-2622) and the double danda (x 2875-2913) is about 253px, some six times a normal word space.

readers.boundary_interpretation: The sirorekha never fully breaks inside a printed word on this line: projecting rows 1951-1968 column-wise, the within-word minimum is 10-16 inked rows out of 18 and never 0, so headline breaks could not be used to cut words. I therefore cut on white gaps in the below-headline body: inter-word gaps measure 39-46 px (409|449, 566|607, 678|720, 1210|1249, 1431|1470, 1744|1784, 1903|1942, 2015|2061, 2563|2606) while every gap inside a word is <=22 px. Word list (0-based): 0 dhiitii x187-409, 1 vaa x449-566, 2 ye x607-678, 3 anayanvaaco x720-1210, 4 agram x1249-1431, 5 manasaa x1470-1744, 6 vaa x1784-1903, 7 ye x1942-2015, 8 avagraha+vadannrtaani x2061-2563, 9 danda x2606-2622, 10 double danda x2875-2912, 11 numeral x2961-3009, 12 double danda x3059-3095. readers.notes: MAGNIFICATION: read the two supplied ~1:1 segment crops first, then measured the source raster directly with PIL (row and column ink profiles at grey threshold 128, plus 8-connected component extents), then re-rendered my own crops of the same line from the same leaf at 2.8x to 12x for visual confirmation of every mark and carrier. Component geometry was re-run at thresholds 150 and 170 in case a faintly inked mark was being lost; nothing new of accent shape appeared. MARK MORPHOLOGY: the six anudattas are 36-39 px wide and 9-11 px tall, fill 0.76-0.92 - dense flat dashes, distinctly wider than tall. The four svaritas are 9-12 px wide and 30-36 px tall, fill 0.85-0.96 - narrow uprights, each standing on the right-hand stem of its consonant. A column-by-column pixel map confirms all four svaritas are the same object; two of them (x2172-2182 and x2538-2547) merge with their word component only because the sirorekha itself drifts about 5 px lower toward the right end of the line, not because they are letter parts. REJECTED FALSE POSITIVES, by shape: (1) the anusvara over gram at x1399-1420, 22x24 px, h/w 1.09, a filled lozenge - a dot about as wide as it is tall, not an upright stroke. (2) Six above-headline vowel signs, all wide and curved, 54-69 px across, h/w about 0.5: ii over dhii x229-283, ii over tii x338-391, e over ye x609-667, o over co x1122-1190, e over the second ye x1944-2001, i over the final ni x2463-2522. (3) The da tail in vadan, x2239-2265, 27x20, fill 0.38, curved and continuous with the body. (4) The r-vocalic descender under the nnr conjunct, x2300-2344, 45x39, fill 0.60, a curved hook continuous with the body - not a straight dash. (5) Sub-10 px specks: x2432-2437 at the foot of the aa-stroke in taa, and several 2-8 px fragments at y>=2091 which are the truncated tops of the NEXT line's glyphs. (6) The faint grey shapes between the danda (x2622) and the double danda (x2875) are verso show-through: no pixel there falls below grey 170. LINE ATTRIBUTION: the central trap does not bite on this line, and I verified that rather than assuming it - rows 1859-1915 are line-wide zero ink, so there is no line-above bar band in my gutter at all. Everything I counted below the body sits 25-52 px under my own baseline and 42-95 px above the next line's first ink. THE ONE HARD CALL: the anudatta at x2293-2329 sits at y2077-2086, about 16 px lower than the other five bars (y2059-2072). I accepted it because (i) its shape is an exact twin of the other five (37x10 px, fill 0.92), (ii) it is bounded by line-wide zero-ink rows 2075-2076 above and 2087-2090 below, so it is a free-standing mark and not the tail of the r-hook that ends at y2074, and (iii) it cannot belong to the next line, whose first ink is at y2091 and whose own bar band would lie near y2240. The obvious explanation for the drop is that the printer had to set it clear of the r-vocalic hook immediately above it. READING NOTES: the standalone a is read per the fount note - it looks like shra or vocalic r in this 1856 type - and it occurs twice, at x720-824 and x1249-1353. Short i versus long ii was decided by which side the matra's vertical sits on: right for ii (dhii: arc 229-283 with its vertical at 272-285), left for i (ni: arc 2463-2522 with its vertical at 2464-2477); that distinction is what makes the upright at x2538-2547 an accent rather than an ii-stem. The least certain glyph on the line is the stacked conjunct at about x2258-2344, which I read as half-na over na with the r-vocalic sign below (nnr); at 12x it shows two stacked na-like elements, a stem, and the hook. I did not reconstruct the line from memory; where the ink and expectation could have diverged (the mark over gram, which at low magnification looks like an accent) I followed the ink and recorded it as anusvara. The terminal numeral is a closed bowl with a straight stem descending on the right, i.e. 1, not 9. As printed there is a wide blank of about 250 px (x2622-2875) between the single danda and the double danda; I have written it as a single space.
